headline: ETF cost-base adjustments are widely misunderstood and almost universally being done incorrectly by Australian investors
reasoning: Navarre explains that every ETF issues an annual member statement (AMIT statement) that adjusts the cost base of all parcels held — not just those purchased in the current year. Most investors are unaware that these adjustments are retroactive and must be applied to every historical parcel. A decade-long dollar-cost averager could have 120+ parcels all requiring annual retroactive adjustments. Failure to apply these adjustments means investors are calculating their capital gains incorrectly and potentially misreporting to the ATO.
quote: So every year, they will either adjust your cost base up or they'll reduce your cost base down. And that's dependent on things that happened inside the fund. It's not really that important why it happened. The fact is they happen and you have to do something about it. Another important fact is you don't have any control over it. No, these things happen in the ETF and you don't know that they're going to happen and you can't influence them in any way... if we go through to say year five and you have your member statement, that now affects all 60 parcels proportionately. So the first year's worth of parcels have now been adjusted five times and that cascades every single year, member statement retroactively updates them all.
